haiku-low.q1: If reports.row_count is 10,000 or fewer, the API streams the CSV in the click response. Above 10,000, it records an export row, queues a job, answers 202, and the job emails a 24-hour download link.
haiku-low.q2: The user gets the already-active export back as 202 with its export_id and status. No new row or job is created, even if the filters differ. A short page message is an open question.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link works for 24 hours. The exports bucket deletes each file 7 days after creation, and abandoned multipart uploads after 24 hours. There is no cleanup job.
haiku-low.q4: Up to three attempts, with waits of 60 s and 300 s, each killed after 1800 s. After the last failure, the row becomes failed with an error, and a failure email is sent. The user can start a new export.
haiku-low.q5: Report rows are read only from the read replica. Export state is stored on the primary database, in the report_exports table.
haiku-low.q6: In the report_exports row on the primary database. The page polls GET /api/reports/{id}/export every 5 seconds while queued or running, and reloads show the stored state.
haiku-low.q7: It streams in 2,000-row pages into an in-memory buffer of about 8 MB, uploading each full buffer as a multipart part. It never holds the whole report, so memory stays far below 512 MB.
haiku-low.q8: Parts are not visible until complete_multipart succeeds, so no partial file is downloadable. On an exception the upload is aborted. A crash skips abort and the bucket's 24-hour rule discards the parts. The next attempt restarts from the beginning.
haiku-low.q9: They are stored as the filters and cols snapshot on the report_exports row, taken at click time. The job payload carries only export_id, and the job reads filters and cols from the row.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on report_exports for (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running, on the primary database. The second insert is rejected and the existing active row is returned.
haiku-low.q11: The file must be fully uploaded and status set to done first. Then the signed URL is made and the email sent. If a rerun finds done with notified_at set, it returns. If notified_at is null, it only sends the email.
haiku-low.q12: Nothing is stored, so there is no partial state or retry. Headers were already sent, so the connection is cut mid-body, the browser treats it as a failed download, the error is logged, and the user can click again.

sonnet.q1: The API reads reports.row_count at click time (unfiltered total). 10,000 or fewer: synchronous, the response to the click is the CSV, streamed (text/csv attachment, chunked, no job, nothing stored). Above 10,000: an export row is recorded, a background job is queued, the API answers 202 {export_id, status}, and the job builds the file in the exports bucket and emails the user a download link valid 24 hours.
sonnet.q2: The unique partial index rejects a second row. The API selects the existing active export and returns it as-is (202 with {export_id, status}), no new job, even if the filters differ. Exception: if that row is queued, has no job_id and is older than 2 minutes, it is treated as a dead click and a job is queued for it now. The Download button is also disabled while a large export is active.
sonnet.q3: The signed link works 24 hours (86,400 s), counted from when the email is sent. The exports bucket deletes every object 7 days after creation (and discards uncompleted multipart uploads after 24 hours). There is no cleanup job.
sonnet.q4: At most 3 attempts (waits of 60 s and 300 s before attempts 2 and 3; each attempt killed after 1800 s). After the last failure, on_final_failure sets the row to failed with an error (unless already done), and sends the report_export_failed email. The page then shows failed (polling stops) and the user can start a new export.
sonnet.q5: Only the read replica, via iter_report_rows. (The primary holds only the report_exports state table, which is not report data.)
sonnet.q6: In the status column of the report_exports row on the primary database (queued/running/done/failed), written by the API and job. The page polls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/export every 5 seconds while queued or running, which reads the user's newest export row from the primary and returns {export_id, status, created_at} (204 if none). Reopening the page does the same read, so it gets the stored state.
sonnet.q7: It streams: iter_report_rows keyset-pages from the replica (about 2,000 rows per page) into an in-memory buffer; at 8 MB the buffer is sent with upload_part to a multipart upload in the exports bucket, the etag is kept and the buffer cleared; the remainder goes as the last part, then complete_multipart. Memory is about one 8 MB buffer, one page and a list of etags (about 113), so it does not grow with report size.
sonnet.q8: On an exception the attempt calls abort_multipart (best effort) and re-raises. If the worker crashes or times out, the abort is skipped and the bucket discards the orphaned parts after 24 hours. Nothing is visible at the key until complete_multipart, so no partial file is downloadable. The next attempt restarts from the very beginning (no progress kept) with a new multipart upload at the same fixed key.
sonnet.q9: They are snapshotted in the filters and cols columns of the report_exports row, inserted at click time (copied from the page URL). The job payload is only {export_id}; the job loads the row by export_id and reads filters and cols from it.
sonnet.q10: A partial unique index on report_exports (user_id, report_id) WHERE status IN ('queued','running') in the primary database. One insert succeeds and the other is rejected, so there is one row and one job.
sonnet.q11: The file must be fully uploaded (complete_multipart succeeded) and the row set to done (UPDATE ... WHERE status='running'); if that updated zero rows and the row is failed, no email is sent. Then the signed URL is made and send_email is called, then notified_at is set. On re-run: done with notified_at set means return (no rebuild, no second email); done with notified_at null means skip the rebuild and only send the email; failed means return.
sonnet.q12: Once streaming has started, the 200 status is already sent, so the error (replica error or 60 s kill) cuts the connection mid-body. No Content-Length and chunked transfer make the browser treat it as a failed download. The error is logged. There is no retry and no partial state is kept. The user can click again.
